questions.text: Do demo players leave in the first three minutes, and from which screen?
questions.decision: Rework the first-run flow if most exits come before the first match starts.

questions.text: Is Fever Tilt played solo against the bot, or by two people on one machine?
questions.decision: Decide whether the bot or local versus gets the next month of work.

questions.text: What do people actually play with, and how many controllers are plugged in?
questions.decision: Decide whether keyboard-only play needs a first-class control scheme.

questions.text: How long does a new player take to reach their first match?
questions.decision: Cut screens before the first match if the median is over a minute.

questions.text: What shape do matches have - which modes, how long, how close?
questions.decision: Tune match length and the default mode.

questions.text: Do players come back on day 1, day 3 and day 7?
questions.decision: Hold the full launch until day-1 return is worth launching on.

questions.text: Does the demo send players on to the wishlist, the full game or the Discord?
questions.decision: Reorder the demo's end screen by what is actually pressed.

questions.text: How often does a session end without a clean exit?
questions.decision: Stop feature work for a stability pass if unclean exits pass 2% of sessions.

questions.text: Which device classes run under 30 frames per second?
questions.decision: Add a low-spec rendering path if the low tier is mostly under 30.

questions.text: Is Time Trial played, and how long do its runs take per track?
questions.decision: Keep, rework or cut Time Trial for the full release.

fixtures.name: first-session
fixtures.about: README §8.3 as the SDK sends it: the Fever Tilt demo, a first session on Windows. Every first_* flag and new_install; two trait bits set on day 0; the time to the first core loop; a session that explored.

fixtures.name: second-session-same-day
fixtures.about: The same install comes back the same day. No flag is set again; the return is paired with the exit node the first session left; only the milestones never reached before are sent; the second core loop is reached by the second loop started.

fixtures.name: returns-across-days
fixtures.about: Day 0, day 1 and day 7 of one install. Each first payload of a day is first_today; the install age rides in the header; the gap in days is a histogram bucket; a trait set after day 0 is ignored, and the day-0 traits ride on every later payload.

fixtures.name: week-and-month
fixtures.about: Monday 2026-11-30 starts an ISO week; Tuesday 2026-12-01 starts a month in the same week. first_week and first_month are each set once.

fixtures.name: crash-then-return
fixtures.about: A session that never ends sends nothing. The next start counts it as an unclean exit, and has no exit node or gap to pair with: what a crashed session would have left is not made up.

fixtures.name: age-cap-and-clock-set-back
fixtures.about: Past day 400 an install is 400 days old. A local day earlier than the latest one seen is the latest one seen: the day never decreases.

fixtures.name: outcomes
fixtures.about: What kind of session it was: a bounce (under a minute, no loop started), deep (three loops completed), and stuck, which only the stream can say.

fixtures.name: inputs-and-frame-rate
fixtures.about: One kind of input is that kind; more than one is mixed. The frame rate sent is the lower median of the most recent 64 samples.

fixtures.name: paused-time-is-not-playtime
fixtures.about: The app in the background is not being played: the time between pause and resume is taken out of the playtime and the session length.

fixtures.name: sentiment-review-feedback-consent
fixtures.about: The pulse, the review request, the feedback form and the share switch are counters like any other: what was asked and answered, never who.

fixtures.name: calls-that-say-nothing
fixtures.about: A metric, label, node, bit or trait the catalog does not declare is ignored, as is an amount of nothing: an SDK never fails the stream.

fixtures.name: values-are-capped
fixtures.about: A counter never sends more than its bound in one payload: 100,000 unless the metric says otherwise. A value far past a histogram's last bucket is in its last bucket.

fixtures.name: a-kilobyte-is-the-cap
fixtures.about: A session that fills every cell passes a kilobyte. The highest metrics are left out, whole, until it fits: here the pause counter and the score margin go, and everything below them is sent.

fixtures.name: star-harvester-stream
fixtures.about: A Star Harvester stream on the Microsoft Store: the Firebase events, as aggregates.

fixtures.name: umlaut-hero-first-song
fixtures.about: An all-ages stream: the microphone ladder, songs attempted and cleared, and the stream's own accuracy score. Nothing acoustic.
